problem_summary.summary: Check whether the tree is a mirror image around its root.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a binary-tree root. Return whether its left and right subtrees mirror each other.

brute_force.explanation: Copy the tree while swapping every node's children, then compare the copy with the original using structural equality.
brute_force.correctness_idea: A tree is symmetric exactly when it is identical to its mirror; the copied tree is constructed by exchanging every left and right branch.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) — the mirror copy and comparison each visit every node once.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) for the copied tree, plus O(h) recursion stacks.

optimized.explanation: Compare mirrored pairs: left-left against right-right and left-right against right-left.
optimized.correctness_idea: Two subtrees are mirrors iff their roots are both absent or have equal values and their outward and inward child pairs are mirrors recursively.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) worst case, stopping early on a mismatched pair.

steps.action: Compare outward pair (1,1) and inward pair (8,8).

steps.condition: Values match and both nodes have no children.
steps.action: Both mirrored child pairs are null; this pair succeeds.

steps.condition: Values match and both nodes have no children.
steps.action: Both mirrored child pairs are null; return true for the whole tree.

edge_cases.handling: Both root child references are null, so it is symmetric.

edge_cases.case: Matching values but missing mirrored child
edge_cases.handling: A null/non-null mirrored pair returns false.
The pair comparison stops and returns false.
